reviews.reviewText: Insanely chill inructor and mo fun I've had in primary. Grades insanely well, ll let you run the flight as you see fit but ll interject and help you out in whatever capacity he can. I do not have enough good things to say about him. He told me to include this in the gouge for him: contact him via his cell before your inrument flights. He wants to discuss the flight plan in advance so nothing comes as a surprise on the day of.

Show up prepared and you'll be fine. She has a great attitude and cares about her students. We need more instructors like this. All gouge isn't good gouge, remember students try to kill IPs all the time. Prepare to laugh and have a good time in the plane if you're doing what you are supposed to.

Super chill reservi, very skilled pilot. Might sound bored. Enjoyable to fly th; very hands-off and teaches well in the plane. Wants you to perform your PSA checkli before every maneuver that requires it (vice ating "3 C's reviewed complete"). Likes to ask "what are the four general things you check for" when you're pre-flighting. If you're doing PELs (not Pattern PELs), he may set you up in a scenario where he wants you to intercept Low Key inead of climbing all the way up to high key. Very fun to fly th; during PA flights he loves to yank and bank and cloud surf so be prepared for lots of high-G turns.____________ -Had him for C4202 and his fir flight th a udent in over 3 months. Pretty chill guy but makes you feel not confident. Very experience pilot but not sure if his time off caused him to forget things, in the brief he asked me queion about the hydraulics syem and I told him that doesn't exi in the syem, He made me pull out the natops and sure enough it wasnt in there, his response "huh mu have changed that".

CNATRA guy, was a 28 inructor until 2018. Takes a minute to warm up to you and has you lead the brief. Briefed hyds syem th him, pulled out my blank diagram, and he told me to put it away and had me brief arting th how one goes about interacting th the syem, arting th pre-flight through engine art-up and then in-flight malfunctions/what you'd see. ll likely ask you some general knowledge queions sprinkled throughout the discuss items. Like he asked me what taxi speeds were (something I haven't looked at since ground school lol whoops) and I totally blanked. Also asked me what the "G" on the aircraft tail is for and I responded "G is for Greatness Sir" and that cracked him up so he does have a bit of a sense of humor (G is the assigned letter for TW4 aircraft). Nice guy overall but I don't think his inructional yle really jived th me. I *did* like that he was very hands-off. Pretty thorough on ADB. Kept harping on me making gradual/"inrument yle" transitions, so if you're comfortable, yeet the plane as you see fit to get yourself configured/in your block. (<- this resulted in me getting airsick for the fir time). Overall a shit flight for me but that was my fault and not his lol. Fair grader and probably gave me nicer grades than I deserved

Fresh out of the FITU. So chill. Let me repeat, so chill. Asks a few thought provoking queions (nothing hard) during the brief and then go fly. Says "cool" after every callout you make. Nothing much else to say. Chose to come back here because he loves to teach udents how to fly. Loves to share his experience in the fleet. Shot the shit in between legs. // Had for aero/night con o/i. Asked how he could have done to inruct better. Loved flying th him, genuinely helpful. Talks more than mo IPs, is ill unfamiliar th some of the fields and courses around here. For the fir time, felt like we were flying "together" if that makes any sense. Would happily fly again. From TX, wreled at TTU, has a little daughter. Augu 21.
Had him for a PA flight. Was very helpful th making comms calls. Very patient.

Mrs. Blanton's husband. Marine C-130 pilot, but transferred to Navy reserves and flies for UPS. Let's you run the brief, very quiet. Same as in plane. Likes talking about fire in flight or on ground so be prepared to get that. Did an O/I th him and warmed up over time, ju break the ice and find something to talk about. Let's you run the flight, but ll help th unfamiliar fields and areas as far as altitudes and frequencies. Control heavy in landings and PELs. Overall pleasant time, would fly th again.

I was his fir flight in the T6 (Jan 2021), cool dude. Was a T34 inructor, currently the Operational Support Officer for the reserve guys (he's ill active) and volunteered to fly th the Boomers again for fun. Expect to do full a NATOPS brief, moly for him to get in the loop th our procedures and not about quizzing you. He's flown in Corpus for years, knows every course rule and airfield like the back of his hand and can help you out if you've never been to a particular airfield before. Bring your procedural knowledge to the plane and he ll give you some cool old school tips and tricks. If your flight was PAs like mine, let him have some fun at the controls and demo uff for you. His techniques are very helpful. Also a chill grader.

Did not get to fly th him; however, he is incredibly laidback and down to earth. Hands down one of the nice inructors around in the squadron. He arted inructing the la week of April and is ill learning the ropes. Brief was light... NATOPS and discussion items, but he did not really ask any queions. He specifically mentioned that he likes to exercise good CRM and has no issue th stching frequencies, bugging heading/altitude, covering radio calls, etc. Overall, he wants to have fun while flying (while keeping things safe) and wants udents to learn something and walk away from the flight th more confidence because of it. Update: flew th him for C4202 and C4203... besides being out of this world chill in the plane and in the brief, he was incredibly generous th grades. Easily my favorite inructor. You should be excited if you are scheduled to fly th him.

Has a TON of hours in the T6. Wants you to be able to discuss FTI procedures in the brief but in the plane, ll teach you other techniques (not in the FTI) for performing maneuvers. Pretty cool to fly th overall. He's a big numbers guy so when preparing for the brief, make sure you can recite any numbers relevant to your discuss items/QOD/profile.

Awesome inructor. Briefed on the phone the night before a 0550 brief time. Only had me NATOPS brief in the morning. Very relaxed and patient in the aircraft. Self described "trim Nazi". Would rather you take an extra minute to be perfectly trimmed prior to executing maneuver. Wants you to have your own method of leaving the block and heading to outlying field, but sugges FMS fir and foremo before descent. Very good about giving short, digeible bits of help in the pattern, vice calling out every deviation and overwhelming you. ll take the controls to show you something, but is ultimately more hands off and learn by experience.

Had him as my onng. He won't have you fill out an EP Limits quiz, however ll expect you to know the notes associated th the limits on the quiz as well as the limits from the NATOPs chapter. Ideally he wants you to have all the EP NWC's down as well. He is a pleasure to fly th and ll fly no matter the weather. As the inrument lead, he loves bugs, OpsChecks, and trimming, and ll take controls from you multiple times during the flight to te your trim. If its not trimmed, have fun going into a UA. Loves to teach, has lots of great techniques, won't quiz you in the plane, and ll show you actual OCF and a PEL into home field for a full op if you ask him to demo it. Great guy, not a super intense brief, fun flights, not the wor grader either.

Very relaxed in the brief and the plane. Likes to talk about topics of intere during ground ops or longer transits. Good at coaching you through a new maneuver and provides helpful feedback in the plane and in the debrief.

Really nice and chill guy. Would like to see udents text the night before and go over a flight plan so the brief is short and you both know what you want to accomplish. He's huge on CRM aka he's always offering to make radio calls, stch frequencies, or bug headings for you. He's also very encouraging and gives positive feedback when you do good headword/SA uff. Gives easy emergencies for PELs and PEL/sos because he wants you to focus more on the flying. If you make a miake on one he won't dock you for it he'll ju let you try again and says "no harm no foul". Is by no means a Santa clause th grades but is a great teacher and fun to fly th

Concur th the above comments. He would frequently stch frequencies or bug a new heading/altitude if directed by ATC while I was in the middle of a turn or some other task that required any amount of attention beyond raight and level flight. Okay on the grading but definitely doesn't ju hand out good grades.

Know your discuss items well, brief is pretty straightforward! For instruments likes to se see you get ahead of your ABCD along th a few ops checks (4~5 is gold)! Not afraid to give a 5 if you kill the setup and final approach, big thing is staying ahead of the aircraft and CRM (doesn't mind if you ask him to bug a HDG/ALT). Super chill overall!!

Super nice, fairly raight forward brief. Didn't really ask much besides the discuss items and didn't go very far into the EPOD. If you're doing well on everything, ll let you know conantly that you're doing a good job. For early inrument flights he likes to bug the headings/altitudes for you as soon as ATC assigns them. Hes a CNATRA guy. One of my favorite IPs so far.
Awesome inructor, let's you make miakes in the hopes that you catch them on your own. Quiet in the plane. Asked almo nothing in the brief. Super relaxed flights th a short but helpful debrief.

ill a little salty cause he failed me on an aero recheck for a bad Cuban 8 and even noted on my grade sheet that my low work was very good considering crossnds. Was kinda pissy in the brief, but it was a 0520 and I've heard he actively hates being on the alpha line and ju isn't a morning person. In the plane I thought he was fine. Gave me a contact UA at the top of my loop, do be ready for that.

Brand brand new, chill in the brief. Lets you run the flight, ll go over the maneuvers after on what needs to be corrected // Brief is average in length and depth. Quirky personality that shows in his teaching yle. Tends to give frequent, borderline intrusive reminders whenever you're about to do something he thought you forgot, so quicken your pace much more than usual to ay way ahead of the plane whenever you're flying th him. Occasional control inputs. Recommend verbalizing all of your procedures along th anything you put into the UFCP/FMS, as well as anything you're planning to do in a few minutes.

C4701/F4103: Extremely chill guy. Encouraging in the plane and gives good tips. Can be a bit quiet, and may ask some specific/nuanced questions in the brief, but does not get upset if you do not know them. Very llling to take controls in the pattern to demo things or give you a break. I enjoy flying th him. Fair/generous grader.
Very chill. Had him for forms check ride. gives good correction tips, and stays calm through the flight.

Awesome IP, love Poo Bear (ask him the story). ll push you in the breif to find your knowlege limit but is very gentle and helpful in doing so, really wants to see people succeed. ll throw weird scenarios at really good students, simulated PMU fail at the 90, simulates getting sleepy on an apporach where he has controls, expecting you to say something and speak up. I know its not very helpful to just say hes a great guy but if youre reading this and youre on the sked th him, just know you'll have a good day.

One of my favorite IPs. As a Cobra pilot he might come across as aggresive, but he's actually a really nice guy and if he tells you you're an idiot, he probably means it in a nice way. Very much lets you run the brief and doesn't ask many queions if you cover all the points. HUGE on teaching people early to make decisions. Even in a 4200 block contacts flight, he wants you to make decisions and if its dumb he'll tell you. Don't ask him what we should do, ju tell him we're gunna do this, and he'll appreicate it. Very much second the fly it like a cadillac.

Expects you to know NWC's nearly verbatim also need to know non memory items for discussion items / EP of day. and can be a bit tough on grading. // Gruff and outspoken, perhaps the mo relaxed IP you'll have the pleasure of working th. Might ask you to brief over the phone, and mo likely ll not have queions for you after. Expect to make new plans on the fly to comply th his suggeions. Very enjoyable to fly th; if you're doing well overall, he ll grow heavy on CRM closer to the end of the flight. Pays close attention to basic airwork to 50 feet deviations, but doesn't seem to consider other errors as tightly. Prefers that you "review/complete" certain checklis during heavy comm activity. Flies based on feel or pilot's intuition to such a degree that may deviate slightly from the FTI, but ll help your underanding of the plane. Very approachable and talks th you like he's known you for years in the debrief, giving many pointers to fine-tune your skills. Felt more like a bro than an inructor. // I also really enjoyed flying (checking) th him. If you can brief the EPOD/QOD verbatim along th any associated "fun fact" paragraphs in the NATOPS it ll go a long way. Very patient in the plane. Doesn't like doing any checklis on the roll except for the Taxi checkli. He really likes it when udents call their own waveoffs inead of him prompting you ("If you're not sure if you're going to land on speed, on centerline, wave off. I'll never give you a hard time if you wave off a landing you're not 100% sure about.") Prefers that udents "fly like a Cadillac;" likes smoother, more deliberate control inputs vice yanking and banking.
Had an aero flight th him, if you do a maneuver well he'll say "that was fuckin sick". Prior Marine crew chief, nice guy, cool in the plane.

Was his fir flight th an SNA. Pretty chill guy and didn't ask much in the brief. Likes to talk through the EP of the day and how you would actually handle it in real life verse ju rattling off what the NATOPS says. Super light on controls. Average grader. The guy knows his FTI uff and expected FTI numbers and what not while flying (makes sense coming raight from FITU).
Super nice guy and wants you to succeed. seems like he loves life and his job. ll coach you if needed but is more than happy to let you run the flight. Need more inructors like this.

June 2023. Concur th above joker/bingo sentiment. Super awesome to fly th. Big chiller. Helps you out th CRM when you're ruggling a bit but overall ll let you handle what you can on your own and wants you to succeed.

Super chill reservi. Flies 737s for American. Really chill and enjoyable inrument O/I experience th him. Expect to lead the brief but he won't dig very deep. Fairly bookish when it comes to FTI procedures but not to the point of impracticality (he won't make you get ATIS tce if you're shooting an approach to CRP followed by one to NGP.) Later commented on good use of CRM). Debrief is thorough and highly conructive. Glorifies what you did well while also giving helpful techniques, focal points to work on for future events.

Very chill to fly th. He's a great pilot and is very good at flying aero (and he likes it a lot), despite him being a reservi and not getting to fly it so often. Even though CTS for altitude may be +/- 100ft, if you're off by a consient amount (ex. you fly 80ft high +/-10ft, you're ill in CTS) he'll get on you for that ("we're not trying to make GOOD pilots; we're making the BE pilots in the world")

Totally different person than sim Harvey. For an inrument in/in, brief was fairly short. He was basically satisfied after a few minutes of me shong I was prepared for the discuss items and had a logical plan for the flight. Quiet in the plane but heavy on controls. Respectful and deliberate, if not a bit soft-spoken. Holds you to the book rictly but ll exercise discretion if you fuck up.

I had him for a 4203 a couple months after he's been in 27; incredibly nice, loves to dig during the brief. He has some obscure numbers from NATOPS down so if you know those he'll love it. during the flight, very very heavy on the controls, didn't seem to be a fan of 60AoB. Not only is he heavy on the controls, but if he wants to make an input he'll art to make it and forget to tell you, which he recognizes he mentioned he's working on getting better th that. Really nice guy, and very chill in terms of personality, likes to get really in the weeds during the brief. Know verbatum Course Rules for Goliad , the 5 reasons for a discontinued entry, and what aircraft and energy ate you need to be at when you're number upnd departing. I enjoyed flying th him (C4204 flight), but he is pretty control-heavy to the point where I had to ask multiple times who had controls. Would say we both weren't on our A-game, as we departed the working area when he had controls (I asked him if we were clear to depart and he thought I was referring to the bottom of the block as we neared 6000' inead of the lateral confines), and one of the upid things I did was line up for the initial for north flow when we were going to south flow. I was on autopilot after going north flow all week and didn't notice until after I called the wrong initial and Tower called us saying WTF, and even then I had to say "hey sir I really fucked up" to get his attention to help me fix it. Think we both ju had an off-day, but remember that IPs are humans too/ no rank in the cockpit. If you have him for a flight please make sure to update this gouge because he is new and I don't want this to be the laing opinion of him.

Down to earth instructor that wants to see you improve. He ll help you out in the plane th bugs and calls but only if you request it or if you get behind. Big Georgia bulldogs guy, played college football (insert college if it matters) married th a daughter very much wants to finish Friday flights to get home and be th fam. Loves to explore new or off the beaten path airfields and makes the flight a mutually engaging experience. Keep your sa up bc he like to multitask and try to help get you ahead of where you might mentally be tracking. -
Gets super airsick and gets irritated by it. May or may not take it out on udent

chill brief, ll barely say anything in the plane because he wants you to feel confident in what you're doing. th that said, also a very good teacher and ll demo a maneuver real quick if you need help

Fresh out the FitU. Chill brief. I was his fir inrument udent, so we were both learning together. Is super upfront that he's new and appreciates being backed up. Really good to fly th. ll bug headings and altitudes if you ask. I was jacking up quite a bit of uff and he was positive and encouraging throughout. Really awesome IP, not too much but not lacking by any means. Great guy, really enjoyed flying th him. Pretty quiet in the plane. Didn't even brief Night Con // Had him for inrument flights. If you did something wrong, he ll ask you to walk him through that series of events/your thought process. He ll also glorify whatever you did well, give encouraging commentary, and ask you to critique him as an inructor to close out the debrief. Fair grader. Good teacher th a genuine personality

Pretty solid inructor, asked a couple of queions in the brief and other times I've had him asked zero queions. Nothing too crazy in the plane, his debriefs are great though. Basically re teaches you everything you did wrong to find any cracks in your procedures that may be leading you the wrong way. Had him for RI's

Extremely chill IP, really wants you to succeed. As long as you crush the brief you could have a terrible flight and he'll ill be totally cool. However, while he's super chill ensure you maintain a rict sense of professionalism th him. He likes to give simulated fuel px and high fuel flow pa the initial at Goliad. For pattern Ps expect chip, oil, or fuel px. For all recovery he likes a very aggressive recovery between 16 and 17.9 units of AOA. He likes when udents use bugs for speed, altitude, and headings. If you feel task saturated he'll help th frequencies and bugging if you ask- ju be sure to preface that you're doing this to ensure good airwork and SA. Unlike all recovery he appreciates a slower, more relaxed recovery for CUAs. However, be fa th PCL idle and speed brake for nose low and PCL max for nose high. Likes to see good use of speed brake. Likes to hear 2-3 ctaf calls while maneuvering to the initial at Goliad. // very good at teaching very specific debrief th tips to actually correct the things you do wrong. Can be heavy on the controls but it's not annoying at all because whenever he's making inputs th you he's verbalizing what he's doing and why he wants you to do it so it's super helpful

Hands down the be IP I've flown inruments th. Super chill in the brief. Go in to the brief prepared and eager to learn (not inn the way that he'll make you queion everything) but he'll bring in his queions and experience in the fleet vs flight school. I learned so much in that brief. He's super humble, and is here to help you learn. As long as you demonrate that you have the desire to learn and the motivation to grow as a udent, you'll be set. sh I would have flown th him earlier. Rockin.

Reservi. Also flies for Southwe. Former marine. Brief= pretty chill. Flight= very fun and chill. He likes to have a good time and is reassuring letting you know when you did well and corrects you when you do something wrong in the nice way possible.

So tall, I'm surprised he fits in the cockpit. raightforward brief, overall very relaxed in the plane. ll sometimes lay out his andards to get a 5 on maneuvers and won't mind you asking. Heavier on the controls on landing (also probably b/c it was night contact flight). Also, fairly quiet. Had to ask him what he ju said several times. 2) Operates at a slower, more easygoing pace than mo inructors.

Can concur, very very tall boi. Extremely relaxed in the brief once you demonrate a basic knowledge of the disucss items. Hit him th NWCs off the bat and it's almo certainly going to be a discussion from then on. Very relaxed in the plane, and creates an environment that's conducive to learning. Is heavy on controls during some landings to the point where I wasn't sure how much I was actually flying, but fairly light on everything else. Overall phenomenal experience flying and briefing th him.

Fresh out of FITU. Loves CRM, only had him on an inrument single in fir block so he didn't expect a lot but loves when you keep calling things out to him like what comes next or your plan of action at the next ep. Use your heading and altitude bugs conantly. Brief was decent ju hit the main points and he was ready to go fly. In the plane hit me th a couple gotchas ju to check SA like calling the wrong MDA to make sure I was confident in what I briefed or was paying attention to my approach plate before I descended to the wrong altitude. Didn't actually get to fly the event th him, got ACN/A'd before we could even brief. That being said, Sir was awesome to talk to, basically just chatted for another 40ish minutes after we'd already determined we wouldn't be flying. Very laid back, hope to get to fly th him in the future.

Do not text him the night before for contacts flights. Would argue again the follong gouge. Had a good brief th him for 4202, didn't interrupt anymore than other IPs to ask queions, wasn't particuarly erd during the NATOPS brief either. He'll raight up tell you in the plane he sounds mean over ICS and doesn't mean anything personal by it. I didn't have a great flight but that wasn't due to him; he was pretty chill in the plane and very hands off. Know your uff and you'll be fine. Had a good debrief and ll answer queions. // Keeps the brief short..... Lombardcatelli LOVES to cut you off while you're briefing. He sometimes can ask weird queions too. He talks really fa. And be prepared for him to scratch your whole plan and ju do what he wants to do. ern demeanor, ll unflinchingly are you down the entire time you're giving the NATOPS brief, and sometimes speaks in such a manner that leaves you uncertain what ll happen next. NWC working knowledge, but know exact words and numbers when briefing from pubs. his words, "words have meaning let's try to get it right" even if you misspeak and its obvious based on everything else you have been saying. Chill at some moments in the plane, but can get irritated quickly and it shows

ll ask for NWC anytime an EP comes up (6 on my 4201). Asks inflight generator limits in order to see if you're udying limits only from the Quiz. ll ask Uncommanded Power Changes... EP th NWC to judge your EP knowledge. Points out any deviation whatsoever from ground procedures, down to the very word. Be 100% familiar th change 1 Hollywood checkli. Generally unpleasant to fly th. // Great in forms. I had some unpleasant experiences th him beforehand and wasn't expecting much, but he was actually a cool dude. If he can tell you've read the (shitty) FTI and are trying hard he gives great pointers, helps out and wants you to succeed.

Absolute Chillmoner, ill learning the ropes, asks some quick EPs, likes to work together in the plane and see new things. Grades fairly, sarcaic, super cool, super tight, one of us ju a little older and ser. Make sure to sound cool on the radios. Loves it if you have good fuel management and weather analysis. Brief was super quick though. Ju know your shit, prepare for where you're going and what you're doing. Looks like Jaime Lannier. Had for fir inrument flights. Fresh out of the FITU as of JUN21. Seemed pretty cold to me in the brief and ju had the other udent talk about the discussion items, but became very nice once I spent some time th her. She is awesome. Married to a civilian and had a kid about a year ago. New out of the FITU and said she came out th a lot of "udent Appreciation Flights" lol. Cares about you learning above all else. September 2024 - I definitely think Mr. Garrecht is overlooked. First of all, if you are feeling under the weather in any way, please respect that he is protecting himself and his family from germs and sicknesses, and do not show up. Don't sit too close (sit at opposite corners of the briefing space). Just come prepared. Know the information per the FTI for whatever your discussion items are, and be familiar with the numbers, speeds, angles of bank, etc. He tends to ask questions in a "fill in the blank" format, which gave me more time to find the answer as he asks the question, because I learned it the same way he asked it. Again, he's hyper-aware of the germs within the OFT or UTD, so be mindful of the small space. Know that he will take the time to wipe everything down again to protect himself and his wife, so please do your best not to cough in this small space. To me, he is helpful and wants you to do well; just be receptive during the sim event and agree with what he's telling you, as he is, in fact, quoting the FTI verbatim. Make whatever corrections he points out and move on. The debrief was nice and insightful, and he reminds you to be a safe pilot while reiterating some key points from what you went over.

Chill in the sim; will hit your grades for mistakes but won't reward your success // Brief was relatively light as he played on his phone while I "told him all I know" about the discuss items, though your mileage may vary. As long as you know your stuff he's a very laid-back guy in my experience, both during the sim and the brief. Feb 2025 I3202 (IUT Event, prior P-8A instructor) - Makes my top 5 most miserable events ever, including my entire time upgrading throughout the fleet squadron. Me: "What did you fly, sir?" Him, completely serious: "Ask a better question." I then asked what squadron he belonged to in his fleet tour, and he proceeded to regale me with tales of how awesome he is and how he got to fly 15 different helicopters in 4 years. This set the tone for the entire event. He is right, even when he's not. Best advice I can give is to take a deep breath when he says something to rile you, which he will. His tone sucks throughout the whole brief and event, and he will teach techniques of his as if they were NATOPS, then tell you that it's just a technique. Some of them are useful, some are not. You will probably not know where you stand with him until the debrief. Debrief was decent and he grades fairly, but I found myself off of my game the entire event because he was being an asshole. Attempted to give constructive feedback on his instructional style when he asked for it, but he immediately made excuses. Biggest thing he will teach you is what you DO NOT want to be like as a pilot. Don't be him!
Will sometimes tell you to ignore dual concurrance so he can just play on his phone. Schedule doesn't say it, but he's a Retired Marine Major.

WARNING: Will throw non-standard things on the profile to teach as much as she can to you. Don't let it throw you off your game.

Patient in the sim and understanding of mistakes, will help by giving hints as to what you can fix on the fly. He was kinda rude in a contacts sim for the landing pattern and if you're flying badly he'll trash you in the debrief. Instruments he was way more chill but I was also way better at flying by then, so he may just have high expectations even for new students.

During the sim he is an excellent coach and pays attention to how closely you abide by FTI numbers and procedures, though he may not catch all your mistakes. Thorough and genuinely helpful debrief complete with in-depth gradesheet commentary. Above-average grader. Adheres closely to CTS; though if you impress him enough overall he won't grade you down for some errors, but will leave advice on the gradesheet. Had him for C3401, he used to only teach instruments. Felt great up until I saw the gradesheet, told me I had a great flight and he was impressed. I'm not sure if I did something wrong during the brief, maybe had him on a bad day, or maybe he entered the grade sheet wrong, but I got 3'd on everything except my actual manuevers, with no comments. I'm not sure how brief/BA/comms etc are 3'd but manuevers can be 4'd? Up until this point I've been 4's down the board with a 5 sprinkled in here and there kinda guy. Overall, counting it as a fluke and would agree with everthing said above. He was great in the sim and brief was chill. I hate it when disgruntled people come on here and bitch,not trying to do that. doesn't teach well, will micro manage your flight and "coach" constantly which might mess your flow during aero or stalls. strict grader and he'll do most of the talking in the brief. Fair grader though.

Will bring to your attention things you missed or did incorrectly but in my experience that didn't effect my grade, just my disposition at the time. But it is an experience and you will probably have above MIF on everything.

Grumpy old dude that expects professionalism and pure business throughout the entire event - brief to sim to debrief. However - extremely condescending to every single question you ask - even ones that pertain to pure technique not referenced in the FTI. That being said, he does seem? Like he cares about making you a better aviator with him strictly being business. Will crack oddly timed jokes that you can't tell if he's just trying to catch you off guard or genuinely lightening the mood. As long as you don't royally screw up he'll pretty much give you straight 4s. Overall - 5/10 instructor.

Is genuinely happy whenever you perform ops checks. Do them at regular intervals for a 5. *long, soft inhale* "Gooooooooooood Blinkerrrr" // Distinctively slow paced, but exceedingly meticulous. In late block sims he may take over your brief, give you ATIS information and clearance in the briefing spaces for you to write down, saving time. Smiles frequently; very pleasant personality and unparalleled patience in the sim to the point that it is difficult to imagine him being angry. Above average grader especially with ops checks. He will notice everything you do wrong and note it in the debrief but not in mean way.

great instructor. he'll be impressed if you do well on brief. will give great advice at your flying to better your technique. very forgiving and you might get a 5 of your knowledge is great.

Excellent instructor. Brief is informative and there are no stupid questions. Agree with excellent upside down writing skills.

This is as of OCT2021, flew I3203 with him and I can say i did not see the man that some of the gouge underneath says he is. 0650 brief and he came in smiling and happy drinking coffee. Guy that said "gg" below sounds like he didn't know what he was doing and so he had a bad sim but blames Major Torres. Classic.

Okay this guy was actually great. Fair grader, will give you over MIF for 80% of the items.
